blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Data selection is critical for training large language models on
massive and heterogeneous corpora. Meta-learning for Training-data Selection offers a principled alternative to heuristic scoring by learning data
weights from a target validation objective, but existing methods face a
trade-off between fine-grained valuation and transferability to unseen data.
A natural solution is to replace per-sample weights with a selection network.
However, we find that directly incorporating such a network into existing MTS
objectives leads to unstable optimization and poor generalization, caused by
weight suppression and persistent reliance on easy-to-learn features. To
address these issues, we propose Transferable Example Scoring and Selection (TESS), a scalable data-selection
framework built on a Pointwise Value Matching objective (PVM). Experiments on LLM safety and targeted instruction tuning demonstrate
strong transfer across datasets, from subsets to full corpora, and from
smaller to larger models.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
The performance of modern AI systems is fundamentally shaped by the training data ( Zha et al., 2025 ; Kumar et al., 2024 ; Zha et al., 2023 ; Whang et al., 2023 ) . For large language models (LLMs), scaling requires assembling massive
corpora from heterogeneous sources ( Zhou et al., 2025 ; Weber et al., 2024 ; Langlais et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2024a ) , which often introduces redundant and
low-quality examples. Training data selection is hence an important component of LLM training.
Many existing methods rank training examples by manually designed scores, such as entropy ( Li et al., 2026 ) , instruction-following difficulty ( Li et al., 2024b ) , reducible training loss ( Mindermann et al., 2022 ) , and distance to target domain ( Deng et al., 2026 ; Min et al., 2026 ) , to name a few. These scoring rules lack the ability to dynamically adapt to new scenarios. Though each captures a potentially useful signal, it remains an open question how these scores may be combined to create more powerful ranking mechanisms.

However, this overlooks heterogeneity among data points in a single domain and cannot generalize to new data domains.

blocks.en: One intuitively appealing idea is to train a meta-network that outputs w i w_{i} for every data point. If the meta-network can generalize to unseen data points, we would be able to train on a small dataset and perform data selection on a much larger dataset, which would also substantially improve efficiency and scalability. Though the meta-network approach has been used by Shu et al. (2019) ; Du et al. (2026) ; Calian et al. (2026) , no such generalization has been reported, not even for the extraordinarily large-scale experiments of Calian et al. (2026) . Perhaps unsurprisingly, our experiments find simplistic training of the meta-network leads to unstable optimization (Figure 2 ) and poor generalization (Table 1 and 3 ).

blocks.en:
Given the massive success of deep learning, the failure of the meta-network to generalize to unseen data is especially perplexing. Our analysis traces the
failure to two properties of the training loss. First, as training progresses, most predicted data weights are suppressed toward zero. As a result, over time, the meta-network loses the ability to distinguish useful training data from harmful training data. Second, the loss causes the network to exclusively learn easy features and ignores hard feature, so the network becomes susceptible to shortcut learning.
blocks.zh:

未能达到训练损失的两个属性。 首先,随着培训的进展,大多数预测的数据权重被压制到零。 因此,随着时间的推移,元网络失去了区分有用的培训数据与有害的培训数据的能力. 第二,损失导致网络完全学习了容易的特性而忽略了硬特性,因此网络变得容易被快捷学习.

blocks.en:
To improve the scalability and generalization of MTS, we propose Transferable Example Scoring and Selection (TESS). At its core, TESS simplifies ScaleBiO ( Pan et al., 2025 ) and introduces a simple mean squared error objective, which we call Pointwise Value Matching (PVM). TESS constructs sample-level pseudo-labels that capture
the utility of training data points and uses these values as supervision for the data-selecting meta-network. Compared to the existing loss, the PVM loss is less focused on easy features, which curbs shortcut learning and promotes generalization.
Further, TESS removes the requirement of ScaleBiO to simultaneously train two LLMs with the meta-network, cutting peak memory footprint by more than 20%.
Experiments on LLM safety and targeted instruction tuning demonstrate substantially improved generalization of TESS across three
settings: cross-dataset transfer,
small-to-large model transfer, and subset-to-full-corpus transfer. Our contributions can be summarized as: • We identify and theoretically analyze two limitations of applying the existing MTS training objective to a shared selection network: competitive weight
suppression that undermines the identification of high-quality training data, and persistent
preference for easy-to-learn features that can encourage shortcut learning. • We propose TESS, a transferable data-selection
framework that constructs sample-level pseudo-labels and uses them as supervision to learn a data selection network generalizable to
unseen data. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work that demonstrates generalization to unseen data in MTS.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Meta-Learning Data Selection for LLMs. Scaling meta-learning data selection to LLMs requires efficiency in face of both huge parameter counts ( Pan et al., 2025 ) and dataset sizes ( Xie et al., 2023b ) . Traditional data selection methods ( Ren et al., 2018 ; Shu et al., 2019 ) differentiate through model updates to compute the hypergradient, which incurs large time and space complexity for large models. ScaleBiO ( Pan et al., 2025 ) and SEAL ( Shen et al., 2025a ) focus on scaling to model parameter counts. If data selection can be trained on a small dataset and generalize to unseen data, it would also significantly improve scalability to large datasets. However, such generalization remains a difficult challenge.
blocks.zh: 为 LLMs 选择 Meta-Learning Data 。 扩大元学习数据选择到LLMS,需要面对巨大的参数计数(Pan等人,2025年)和数据集大小(Xie等人,2023年b)提高效率。 。 。 。 。 传统的数据选择方法(Ren等,2018;Shu等,2019)通过模型更新来区分来计算超梯度,这给大型模型带来大量的时间和空间复杂性. scaleBiO (Pan等, 2025年)和SEAL (Shen等, 2025年a)专注于缩放到模型参数计数. 如果能够对数据选择进行小数据集的培训并概括到无形数据,它也会大大地提高大数据集的可扩展性. 然而,这种概括仍然是一个困难的挑战。

blocks.en:
In terms of generalization, existing approaches can be broadly grouped into sample-level, domain-level, and meta-network methods. Example-level methods ( Xie et al., 2023b ; Xia et al., 2024 ; Shen et al., 2025a ; Calian et al., 2026 ) learn one weight for each training data point, thereby offering no generalization to new data points. Domain-level methods ( Xie et al., 2023a ; Xie et al., 2025 ; Pan et al., 2025 ; Yang et al., 2026 ; Wen et al., 2026 ) partition the training data into domains and assign one data weight to each domain. Chameleon ( Xie et al., 2025 ) and Data Mixing Agent ( Yang et al., 2026 ) further introduce a
shared domain taxonomy that enables limited weight sharing among data domains. However, domain-level weights are too coarse to capture the
crucial differences in data quality and content within each domain ( Lee et al., 2024 ) .
Meta-network methods ( Shu et al., 2019 ; Du et al., 2026 ; Calian et al., 2026 ) train a meta-network to output the weight for each data point directly. In theory, this should allow generalization to new data points; in practice, no generalization has been reported. Notably, DataRater ( Calian et al., 2026 ) trains a separate scorer for each dataset,
suggesting generalization across dataset is challenging even when the network are trained with a huge amount of data.
With this paper, we analyze the reasons behind the challenge mathematically and offer a simple, practical, and high-performance solution.

blocks.en:
Shortcut Learning. Shortcut learning occurs when models rely on easy features that are
strongly predictive of training labels but whose correlations
weaken or reverse under distribution shifts, impairing
out-of-distribution generalization ( Geirhos et al., 2020 ; Shah et al., 2020 ) . Prior work distinguishes predictivity , how reliably a
feature predicts training labels, from availability ,
how easily it can be extracted ( Hermann et al., 2024 ) . Scimeca et al. (2021) find that solutions favoring easy-to-learn
cues tend to lie in flatter minima and are more abundant in
parameter space, while Qiu et al. (2024) show that simpler
or more strongly correlated spurious features can slow
core-feature learning. We investigate these dynamics in data selection networks. We show that the ScaleBiO loss continues to reinforce easy-to-learn features that are susceptible to shortcut learning, while our proposed PVM promotes the learning of harder and more transferable features.

The previous subsection links weight suppression to reduced sample
discrimination. We now examine a second limitation: ScaleBiO can continue

remaining prediction error. This distinction matters for generalization
when an easy feature is predictive on the training data but
unreliable on unseen data, thereby acting as a shortcut ( Hermann et al., 2024 ; Geirhos et al., 2020 ) .

blocks.en:
Empirical verification. To test shortcut reliance, we add shortcut features to the seen training
data and flip them on unseen data (Appendix E ). We use the gap between seen and unseen dataset accuracy as a proxy for generalization, with smaller gaps
indicating better generalization on unseen data. Table 1 shows clear
differences in training dynamics. Under both shortcut strengths, TESS with ℒ ϕ PVM \smash{\mathcal{L}_{\bm{\phi}}^{\mathrm{PVM}}} improves unseen accuracy and

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: We introduced TESS, a transferable data-selection framework that learns a selector from sample-level pseudo-labels. We identify weight suppression and easy-feature preference of ScaleBiO objective and address them with PVM. TESS shows strong transfer across datasets, corpus scales, and model sizes.

blocks.en:
For LLM safety, we use Alpaca and Dolly as training datasets and evaluate on DirectHarm4, HarmBench, and HEx-PHI: • Alpaca ( Taori et al., 2023 ; Peng et al., 2023 ) contains
52,002 instruction–response pairs covering diverse
instruction-following tasks. • Dolly ( Conover et al., 2023 ) contains
15,011 human-written instruction–response pairs covering
tasks such as question answering, summarization, and
creative writing. • DirectHarm4 (DH4) ( Lyu et al., 2024 ) contains
400 harmful instructions, with 100 examples in each of
four categories: malware, drugs, phishing, and disinformation. • HarmBench (HB) ( Mazeika et al., 2024 ) evaluates
harmful behavior generation.
Its text-only portion contains 400 behaviors across
standard, contextual, and copyright-related categories. • HEx-PHI (HEx) ( Qi et al., 2024 ) evaluates responses
to instructions spanning prohibited-use categories.
Its original release contains 330 instructions, with
30 examples in each of 11 categories: illegal activity,
child abuse content, hate/harassment/violence, malware,
physical harm, economic harm, fraud/deception, adult content,
political campaigning, privacy violation, and tailored
financial advice.

blocks.en: Appendix G Conclusion
blocks.zh: 附录G 结论

blocks.en:
In this paper, we introduced Transferable Example Scoring and Selection (TESS), transferable data-selection framework that utilize sample-level pseudo-labels to learn a data selection network generalizable to unseen data.
Our theoretical and empirical analyses identify competitive
weight suppression and persistent easy-feature preference
as limitations of the ScaleBiO meta-objective.
To address these issues, we propose a new training objective PVM.
Experiments demonstrate cross-dataset, subset-to-full-corpus,
and small-to-large model transfer.
Specifically, in terms of generalization, TESS outperforms the strongest learnable-weighting baselines by 22.75 22.75 and 3.99 3.99 points on LLM safety and targeted instruction tuning, respectively.
blocks.zh:
在本文中,我们介绍了可转移示例分红和选择(TESS),即可转移数据选择框架,该框架利用样本级伪标签来学习一个可通向无形数据的数据选择网络。
我们的理论和经验分析发现,
减重和持续的易感偏好
作为ScaleBiO元目标的限制。
为了解决这些问题,我们提出了一个新的培训目标PVM。
实验显示跨数据集,子集到全体,
以及小到大模型传输。
具体地说,在一般化方面,TESS的表现分别比最强的可学习加权基线在LLM安全和定向教学调试方面高出22.75 22.75分和3.99 3.99分.
